Let be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the -torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If or if is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. Original abstract

We study skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free -action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.

Let be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every diffeomorphism isotopic to , the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals if and only if . Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For diffeomorphisms, , we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.

Original abstract

Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of [CMU19] to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's -metric that strengthens [Ruh21]. We also establish a local -Hölder bound for the map sending a Hölder potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the -metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem [B25]: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.

Original abstract

We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are , with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for Hölder potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

Original abstract

We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index . Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.

Original abstract

We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lamé system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lamé moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set . The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lamé operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in , together with a generalized exponential attractor.

Original abstract

We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.

Original abstract

We study self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs together with -valued twists that exhaust the second cohomology group of the associated Zappa-Szép product category. We define and analyse the associated universal, reduced, and essential -algebras, along with their Toeplitz versions and core subalgebras. In fact, we develop our theory in the more general setting of -operator algebras, where is any non-empty set of parameters. This includes -algebras, -operator algebras and symmetrised -operator algebras for , as special cases. We use three complementary approaches: twisted inverse semigroups, twisted ample groupoids, and -correspondences. We provide, in terms of the self-similar action, general characterisations of topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, finite non-Hausdorffness, effectiveness, and local contractiveness for the associated ample groupoids. We generalise the classical Cuntz–Krieger Uniqueness and Coburn–Toeplitz Uniqueness Theorems for graph -algebras to twisted -operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions. We characterise when the natural inclusions are Cartan, give checkable criteria for simplicity and pure infiniteness of the essential algebras, and discuss when the universal and reduced algebras coincide. We also provide conditions that ensure the singular ideals vanish. A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. Original abstract

We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.

Original abstract

We consider a class of noisy dynamical systems on the two-dimensional torus whose phase evolution is governed by Mobius transformations. In the deterministic limit, these systems favor phase-locking that is described by the band-gap structure of an associated Schrodinger equation with a periodic potential. We use the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin method to characterize this structure in the slow-fast limit. Then we show that large-deviation theory describes fluctuations of the finite-time rotation number, whereas weak-noise escape actions determine the exponential scale of rare phase slips. These estimates provide quantitative criteria for metastable phase-locking and melting of Arnold tongues over a prescribed observation time. We derive sufficient conditions for stochastic trajectories to follow prescribed canard segments. With controlled entrance errors, exponential amplification of fluctuations along repelling branches leads to an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence in the slow-forcing limit.

We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, ) = Q()/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.

Original abstract

Consider a symplectic surface in a three-dimensional contact manifold with boundary on Reeb orbits (periodic orbits of the Reeb vector field). We assume that the rotation numbers of the boundary Reeb orbits satisfy a certain inequality, and we also make a technical assumption that the Reeb vector field has a particular “nice” form near the boundary of the surface. We then show that there exist Reeb orbits which intersect the interior of the surface, with a lower bound on the frequency of these intersections in terms of the symplectic area of the surface and the contact volume of the three-manifold. No genericity of the contact form is assumed. As a corollary of the main result, we obtain a generalization of various recent results relating the mean action of periodic orbits to the Calabi invariant for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.

Original abstract

This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries. Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincaré-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation. Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in [Mc] to justify the applicability of the Poincaré-Melnikov method.

Original abstract

In this paper, we investigate the time-averaged phase space arclength of a trajectory, expressed through a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, as a trajectory-based diagnostic for distinguishing regular and chaotic dynamics. The proposed indicator, , is computed by integrating the equations of motion together with a single scalar arclength-accumulation equation and therefore does not require variational equations, neighboring trajectories, or spatial derivatives of a Lagrangian descriptor field. Using Birkhoff's ergodic theorem together with estimates for quasiperiodic motion and correlation-based arguments for chaotic ergodic dynamics, we show that regular and chaotic trajectories exhibit different finite-time behavior despite the convergence of in both regimes. For quasiperiodic trajectories with Diophantine frequency vectors, deviations from the limiting average decay as , whereas sufficiently mixing chaotic dynamics exhibit root-mean-square fluctuations of order under suitable correlation assumptions. This difference in finite-time convergence and fluctuation scaling provides the theoretical basis for using to discriminate between the two dynamical regimes. We validate the proposed approach in the Hénon–Heiles and Fermi–Pasta–Ulam systems, comparing the resulting classification of initial conditions with SALI as a reference chaos indicator. The results support as a complementary single-trajectory diagnostic for chaos detection and as a practical source of scalar features for the analysis of trajectory ensembles, particularly in settings involving large numbers of trajectories or high-dimensional systems.

Original abstract

We study the geography of taut foliations on compact -manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on -manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.
